newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Bank Negara quiet on higher 1996 income.
newsitem.headline: Bank Negara quiet on higher 1996 income.

text.p: State-controlled heavyweight Bank Negara Indonesia rose sharply on the Jakarta stock exchange on Wednesday, but bank officials declined to comment on speculation of higher-than-forecast 1996 earnings.
"We cannot comment on that. The result is still in the auditing process, we will announce it soon when it is completed," an investor relations official of the bank said.
He also said the bank had forecast a profit of 326 billion rupiah for 1996 in its initial public offering last year.
The bank was listed on November 25 on the Jakarta exchange.
Brokers said BNI shares traded heavily and made significant gains on Wednesday on continued speculation that the firm would book higher income in 1996.
By mid-afternoon it was up 75 rupiah to 1,625 on a turnover of 67.1 million shares. It was the most active stock on the market.

Brokers also said there was speculation that a management fee of four percent which they said the bank paid from its profits to the government no longer applied since the bank became a listed company.
The investor relations official said it was true the bank used to pay a fee to goverment but not as a management fee.
"It was in a form of a donation for poverty alleviation. The total was not more than 2.5 percent from net profit annualy. But since we become a public company, it stopped," he said.
